summary: Willamette NF lookout in Linn County, Oregon: a ground L-4 cab built in 1935 and burned or removed on site in 1967.

facts.status_note: Register says removed in 1967; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1967; Rex's page says disposed of by burning on site in November 1967

staffing.status: lookouts recorded from 1935 through 1947; no end-of-staffing date in these sources

access.note: Forest Service trail page lists Chimney Peak Trail #3382 in the Middle Santiam Wilderness and describes the rocky peak, where a fire lookout once stood, as a possible goal for adventurous hikers; Forest Service Road 2041 is closed in winter

visit.trail_note: Chimney Peak Trail #3382 starts at a trailhead on the Forest Service Road 2041-646 spur and crosses the Middle Santiam River and Pyramid Creek without bridges

events.note: A trail of 23 miles from the Cascadia ranger station to Chimney Peak and Quartzville, with a telephone line built along it
Chimney Peak named as one of eleven new emergency lookout stations for the Santiam district
August 1934: lookout house to be erected that fall; materials to be packed by mule over 12 miles, then hauled up a 1000-foot aerial cable. September 1934: a NIRA crew was building the house
Register and firelookout.com date the ground L-4 cab to 1935
Daily Capital Journal, August 1935: a lookout stationed there, whose wife planned to spend several weeks with him
Robert Morrow was the Forest Service lookout, per a September 1936 Bend Bulletin item
Robert D. Stumpf to fill the lookout fireman position, per a July 1939 Albany Democrat-Herald item
Phil Cane, lookout at Chimney Peak Station, per an August 1942 New Era item; lightning struck near the station but started no fires
July 1947: Mrs. Roy Timmerman, wife of a lookout at the station, carried down the mountain on a stretcher after an appendicitis attack
Register says the cab was removed in 1967; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1967

Rex's page: disposed of by burning on site, November 1967; a November 3, 1967 engineering memo quoted there names Chimney Peak with two other lookouts whose disposal requests would be submitted promptly
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register April 25, 2011

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The August and September 1934 items describe a lookout house being planned and then built that fall, but the register and firelookout.com both give 1935 as the build year. The record uses 1935 and notes the 1934 construction work.

The register says removed in 1967, firelookout.com says destroyed in 1967, and Rex's page says disposed of by burning on site in November 1967. All three agree on 1967 and differ only on how the cab came down.
The register and firelookout.com give 4,965 feet (1,513 m); a 1939 item gives 4954 feet. The story uses the register figure, which matches the brief's 1513.3 m.

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains on the site today or whether the site is open to the public, so access is omitted. Rex's page is the main source for staffing and the 1967 disposal; its newspaper items are quoted secondhand and were not checked against the original papers. The 1967 memo does not say outright that Chimney Peak was one of the three lookouts burned; the story says it is named with two others whose disposal requests would be submitted promptly. The brief's elevation (1513.3 m) matches the register. The brief's record has no build year or removal year; 1935 and 1967 are added from the register. The Rex page has a 1933 panorama photo note with no image URL, so no photos were added. A search turned up the Forest Service trail page (source 4), which says visitors can climb the peak to where a fire lookout once stood. It does not describe what remains, so the 'today' section says so and access is recorded as public trail access on that page.
